# DocumentedPropertyAssignment

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="info" text="off by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Report a value stored in a property that breaks the property's contract
when PHPDoc is taken into account: the `@var` type of the property rejects
it, or the declared type rejects a value whose type only PHPDoc describes.
PHP may run such an assignment, but the code and its documentation
disagree. Mismatches the code alone proves are InvalidPropertyAssignment's.

## Example

```php{9}
<?php
final class Session
{
    /** @var string */
    public $token;

    public function close()
    {
        $this->token = null;
    }
}
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 9: Assign string to Session::$token, not null.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Assignments, stored values and property resolution as
  InvalidPropertyAssignment defines them: the written class still comes
  from native declarations only.
- The type of the value is the one PHPDoc-aware inference gives:
  `@param`, `@var` and `@return` tags count.
- Every declaration the write may reach rejects every value of the
  stored type, through the declared type of the property or its `@var`
  type.
- The weak-mode conversions and the exceptions of
  InvalidPropertyAssignment apply alike, except that an untyped property
  with a `@var` type is checked.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Assignments InvalidPropertyAssignment reports: the declared types
  reject what the code alone shows.
- A `@var` type naming templates, and a `@var` type the declared type
  rejects (a stale tag).
- The value details of a `@var` type: integer ranges, string lengths
  and literal string values. `@var positive-int` accepts any integer.
- Every exception of InvalidPropertyAssignment other than untyped
  properties.
- `null` stored in a property whose default value is `null`: the
  default makes its `@var` type nullable, as it does for a parameter.

## Fix

None: either the assignment or the documentation is wrong.

## PHP versions

All versions.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "DocumentedPropertyAssignment": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore DocumentedPropertyAssignment
```
